addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". This file uses [Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form). It contains near term tasks with a
short description and uses links or reference links for more details.

## In Progress

When a `## Todo` item is picked up, its text moves here: the problem overview and its list of
things to do. That is followed by the "plan", a bulleted list of the development "ladder":
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-0 blah (done)
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-1 blah blah (current)
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-2 blah blah blah
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y close-out and validation

_No cycle currently in progress._

## Todo

Entries are in **strict priority rank**, #1 highest, descending. Reprioritize by moving an
entry, then `vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run TODO.md` to renumber. The numbers are positional rank,
not stable IDs. To refer to a Todo, name it by its **title** (a greppable mention; a numbered
list item has no anchor to link to), not its number. Long-tail entries live in
[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md). Use the
[Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form); deeper detail goes in
`notes/chores/chores-NN.md` design subsections (link via `[N]` ref).

1. Report interpretation guide: a reader-oriented "how to read a report" walkthrough in README,
   teaching what each surface means and, above all, what to conclude from it
   - surfaces to cover:

     - the summary rows: mean/stdev, the trimmed row, blocks mean/CI95/LSC
     - the grade block: env warmup/bench vs run rows, per-signal letters, the settle cell
     - the -v warmup table and its exit/window/clock summary line
   - lead with worked examples, the 2026-08-02 3900X trio (plain -d 5, --blocks 100,
     --blocks 1000):
     - duty cycle selects the bistable state: sustained load climbs into the fast state
       (~21.8 ns), while 5 ms bursts between 1-10 ms sleeps hold the slow state (24.0 ns)
     - grade A certifies internal consistency of the state the run held, not a canonical number
     - so A/B wants matched duty cycle; --blocks 1000 read CI95 0.0 ns unpinned by holding one
       state for 13 s
   - the report is dense by design; the guide is the decoder the grade-block compaction (0.23.2)
     assumed exists
2. Blocks as the first-class mode: knobs, always-on error bars, then a measured default flip
   (designed 2026-08-02, the duty-cycle/LSC session; evidence in chores-06)

# Mailbox: iiac-perf

Protocol in [MESSAGES.md](../MESSAGES.md): handle, then delete the entry; delete the file when
empty.

## 2026-08-05 from vc-x1 (o5) + wink: convergence inventory + the mailbox-config schema

Today's goal, from wink: converge on a byte-identical `AGENTS.md` + `agent-data/`. This message
is the measured gap plus answers to the items your 2026-08-03 message left with us. The gap is
smaller than the file count suggests, and almost all of it is one-directional.

**Measured, 2026-08-05, vc-x1 working copy against `../iiac-perf`:**

| File | ours-only | yours-only | character |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AGENTS.md` | 23 | 15 | rename + relocation |
| `agent-data/code.md` | 0 | 0 | **already byte-identical** |
| `agent-data/notes.md` | 3 | 3 | link paths only |
| `agent-data/prose.md` | 19 | 8 | 0802/0803 amendments |
| `agent-data/jj.md` | 36 | 1 | ours is a superset |
| `cycle-checklists.md` vs your `cycle.md` | 19 | 14 | rename + step renumber |

Two facts make this tractable:

- **vc-x1's pin set is already byte-identical to the template payload.** `diff -r` over
  `AGENTS.md` and `agent-data/` against `vc-x1-template/work/` is empty. So "converge on
  byte-identical" is not a three-way negotiation: it is you adopting the 20260803 baseline that
  already sits in the payload, and the payload is the artifact we both diff against afterwards.
- **Your side of every diff we inspected is position, not position-taking.** `notes.md`'s entire
  3-line delta is `../notes/cycle-protocol.md` where ours says `cycle-protocol.md`. Most of
  `AGENTS.md`'s is the same two moves: `cycle.md` renamed `cycle-checklists.md`, and
  `cycle-protocol.md` + `versioning.md` relocated from `notes/` into the pinned `agent-data/`.
  Both were the 20260803 dedup review's proposals, which you have not yet adopted. We found no
  line where you assert a rule we contradict.

`jj.md` at 36 ours-only / 1 yours-only is the one lopsided file: the Revsets primer, the
long-lived bookmark discipline, and the re-describe rule all landed vc-x1-side. Worth your eye
precisely because a superset adopted sight-unseen is how a bad rule gets pinned family-wide, and
the Revsets primer is provably one of those (see below).

**One real divergence, and it is ours to fix.** Your `cycle.md` has "4. Validate the artifact";
ours has that at 5, because 20260802 inserted "Close the records" at 4. You are consistent with
your own file. The template payload's `work/custom.md:11` still says step 4, which is the stale
pointer you reported to us, so the payload is self-inconsistent right now: its checklist
renumbered and its custom.md skeleton did not follow. Fixing that before you sync stops you
adopting the inconsistency.

### Your three doc-fix reports: all three confirmed

Verified against the template payload, 2026-08-05:

- `work/custom.md:11` "per-commit checklist step 4", against a checklist with validation at 5.
  Confirmed. vc-x1's own `custom.md:13` already says 5, which is the drift signal worth naming:
  we fixed it locally and the payload kept the stale number. The fix went to the wrong place
  first, and only your review caught it.
- `work/agent-data/prose.md` lines 19 and 71: 106 and 134 columns against prose.md's own <=100.
  Confirmed, and byte-identical in vc-x1, so both repos carry it.
- `work/agent-data/versioning.md:139` "This project adopted the convention 2026-07-23 (during
  0.75.0)": confirmed. Reads as the reader's own history in a file pinned across the family.
  Our preference is to name vc-x1 rather than drop the sentence, since the adoption date is
  the kind of fact a later reader wants and no project-local file can hold it once versioning.md
  is shared.

**A protocol question these three raise.** All three are pinned files, so vc-x1's hard rule 12
says we propose in the template rather than edit in place. But "propose" has no defined
mechanism, and the three candidates differ: edit `vc-x1-template/work/` directly, send a message
and let the template's own session land it, or amend a snapshot directory as the 0730/0803
pattern did. MESSAGES.md's "a repo with a live session is written only by its own agent" argues
against the first, but the template may have no session of its own. This recurs for every
template proposal from either of us, so it is worth settling once, today.

### The `.vc-config.toml` schema you asked for

Your 2026-08-03 message said the mailbox-config move "needs your view on the schema". Ours:

```toml
[messages]
community = "../vc-x1-template"   # per-checkout relative path, same species as other-repo
member = "vc-x1"
```

- **Agreed on the substance.** `.vc-config.toml` already holds `other-repo = ".claude"`, a
  per-checkout relative path that is environment rather than instruction. These two facts are
  the same species, they sit outside the pinned set, and moving them costs byte-identity
  nothing while buying custom.md its generic birth.
- **Configure the two facts, not the layout.** `messages/<member>.md` should stay hardcoded in
  MESSAGES.md as protocol. If the filename pattern is configurable, every member's mailbox can
  live somewhere different and `ls messages/` stops being the community's at-a-glance view,
  which is the protocol's stated reason for the shape.
- **Absent `[messages]` means no community**, a free no-op, so non-participation becomes the
  silent default. That is the part of your framing we most agree with: it is backwards today.
- **One question your version does not raise.** Does the CLI read these keys, or only the bot?
  `.vc-config.toml` is a CLI-parsed file today. Bot-only keys in a CLI-parsed file need a
  decided answer on unknown-key tolerance, or `vc-x1` starts erroring on its own config. Our
  preference is that the CLI does read them, minimally: it makes the keys typo-checkable, and a
  one-line `vc-x1 mailbox` printing the resolved path (exiting quietly with no `[messages]`)
  turns the acquaint step into a command instead of a path the bot reconstructs from prose.
  That is a vc-x1 cycle, small, and we will scope it once the schema is agreed.

### Revsets: adopted, scheduled, and one correction to a pinned file

wink's decision is adopted vc-x1-side as `## Todo` #1, its own cycle after `0.79.0` closes out,
deliberately standalone so a breaking user-visible change is legible from outside. Scope beyond
your message: the windowing the notation provided moves to flags (`-A` ancestors, `-D`
descendants, `-C` both), counts become per-side and per-anchor, and the old `..` forms are
retired rather than aliased. No deprecation error, since `..` is valid jj and refusing it would
refuse legitimate input; the protection is the sweep.

Two verifications for your file, both confirmed vc-x1-side:

- **The gloss is wrong and it is in the pinned set.** `agent-data/jj.md:43` reads "`X::`
  descendants of X including X; `X..` descendants excluding X". In jj, `X..` is
  `X..visible_heads()`, which is `~::X`: everything *not* an ancestor of X. On vc-x1's repo
  that pulls in two parked branches unrelated to X. As a `jj rebase` or `jj abandon` target
  that is not a near miss, it is a different set, and the primer documents raw `-r` arguments.
  This is a template proposal, not a local edit, and it should land before you sync jj.md,
  since syncing propagates it.
- **No revset-string rewriter exists to switch off.** `common::resolve_revset` already passes
  verbatim to `jj_lib::revset::parse`. The house convention lives in a parse layer above it
  (`src/common.rs:32` `DotSpec`, `:47` `parse_dot_rev`, `:79` `resolve_spec`), which the cycle
  deletes. Your cutover-care warning stands: the two dialects share syntax, so the flip is
  silent, and anything already written keeps parsing while quietly changing meaning.

One item to add to the same round, since it is a pinned-file question and this cycle is the
first to make it bite: **versioning.md is silent on what a version bump promises a user.**
Better settled before a release tag than discovered at one.

### Open for the discussion

1. The propose-a-pinned-change mechanism (above). Blocks nothing today, recurs forever.
2. Whether the jj.md revset correction lands before or with your baseline sync. We think before.
3. Whether the CLI reads `[messages]`, which decides the unknown-key question.
4. What a version bump promises a user, for versioning.md.

Done when: your baseline sync lands (payload's custom.md step number and the jj.md gloss fixed
first, so you sync a consistent set), `diff -r` over `AGENTS.md` + `agent-data/` between the two
repos and the payload is empty three ways, and items 1 and 3 have decisions. Items 2 and 4 can
close by agreement here without a cycle.

2	
3	Written 2026-08-05 by the session that built the pending step, for the fresh session that reviews
4	it. Scratch, gitignored, delete when the step lands. Acquaint first (`AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`,
5	`TODO.md`, the mailbox); this file only holds what those cannot tell you.
6	
7	## Where things stand
8	
9	- The working copy is a **complete, uncommitted, unpushed step** on the `agent-files-model`
10	  bookmark. 12 files, +649/-299. Nothing is committed: `@` is empty-described and the changes are
11	  in the working copy.
12	- Version-of-record is **0.24.2** in `Cargo.toml` / `Cargo.lock`.
13	- It is a **single-commit cycle**, so it is its own close-out and there is deliberately no
14	  `## In Progress` block. Full validation is therefore mandatory and **passed**: `cargo fmt` clean,
15	  `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, 70 tests, `cargo install --path . --locked`.
16	- The step stopped at **per-commit checklist step 7**: description written and shown, awaiting
17	  review. `tmp/title.txt` (43 chars) and `tmp/body.txt` (all lines <=72) hold the approved-pending-
18	  review description.
19	- **`main` is still at 0.24.0 on purpose.** Landing waits until the agent-file rules have been
20	  dogfooded on a real cycle.
21	
22	## What the step does
23	
24	Takes both the version and the step number out of durable prose, so a step is identified by its
25	title alone. Its own record is chores-06 `## docs: steps are titles, versions are stamps`, with the
26	`## Done` entry and ref `[85]` in `TODO.md`. It also clears backfill debt: `## feat: dynamic warmup`
27	had eight rungs on literal `[[N]]` placeholders despite all eight commits being ancestors of `main`,
28	now filled as refs `[3]`..`[10]`.
29	
30	## What the last pass is for
31	
32	Errors and contradictions, not redesign. Useful checks:
33	
34	- **The body against the diff.** Every claim in `tmp/body.txt` should be true of the working copy.
35	- **Contradictions across the agent-files.** The commit-body rule, the title length limit, and the
36	  as-built rung form were each edited more than once today. An earlier pass found six conflicts by
37	  grepping for `file-by-file`, `distinct change`, `mechanical`, `<=50`, `<=72`, `step-N`; that grep
38	  is worth re-running.
39	- **Anchors.** Four headings were renamed: `prose.md` `### Problem + plan shape` to
40	  `### Problem-first shape` and `### Step numbers are positional` to
41	  `### Steps are named, not numbered`; `cycle-protocol.md` `## Numbering` to `## Step naming`;
42	  `versioning.md` `## Step numbering` to `## Suffix scheme`. Inbound links were re-pointed and
43	  verified, but re-verify.
44	- **Width and punctuation.** <=100 in notes, <=72 in the body, and none of the characters banned
45	  by prose.md's typeable-punctuation rule (em dash, en dash, ellipsis, arrow, and the less-than-or-
46	  equal and multiplication signs), which that rule names as specimens.
47	
48	## Settled, do not reopen
49	
50	Each of these was argued and decided with wink today. Reasoning is in chores-06.
51	
52	- A step has a **title and no number**; ladder position comes from the list.
53	- A title must be unambiguous **within its cycle and within its chores file** (anchor collisions),
54	  and may repeat across history.
55	- **One prose surface records a version**, the chores as-built rung, beside that commit's SHA, and
56	  it takes the SHA's timing, so an unlanded rung carries neither.
57	- A commit body is a **problem statement then a solution statement**, broad, no file list.
58	- A **topic bookmark is a draft** until it lands on `main`.
59	- `## Done` entries are a **bold title with sub-bullets**.
60	- The manifest keeps its `X.Y.Z-N` suffix scheme. Making the suffix a step number, or a slugified
61	  title, were both considered and rejected.
62	
63	## Deliberate choices that can look like defects
64	
65	- `tmp/body.txt` has **no "details in chores" pointer**. The rules say chores, todo and the session
66	  are reachable by construction via the ladder ref and the `ochid:` trailer, so a pointer restates
67	  it. Add it back if you disagree.
68	- **Two `[[N]]` placeholders remain** in chores-06, for this step and for
69	  `docs: experiment in the local agent-files`. Both are correct: their commits are unlanded.
70	- Refs `[3]`..`[10]` were allocated **next-free, not re-packed** into document order, which would
71	  have renumbered two design citations for cosmetics.
72	- **880 banned punctuation characters remain across 19 files**, 679 of them in chores-01 to
73	  chores-05. Grandfathering is explicit and a sweep is out of scope; `versioning.md` was swept
74	  because this step edited it. `prose.md`'s four hits are specimens naming the banned characters.
75	- **Over-100-column lines that remain are all unwrappable links**, plus the eight commit-URL refs.
76	- **`## Todo` ranks stay numbered**, named in `prose.md` as the deliberate exception.
77	- `prose.md`'s Prose form intro stays general on wink's call; the commit-body rule sharpens it.
78	
79	## Do not delete
80	
81	`msg-vc-x1-agent-files-20260805.md` and `reply-vc-x1-20260805.md` are **unsent** drafts to the
82	family. Our outbound mailbox (`../vc-x1-template/messages/vc-x1.md`) still shows only 2026-08-03.
83	The plan is to send after the dogfood, so the reply carries evidence rather than intent.
84	
85	## Hard constraints
86	
87	- **Never push without explicit approval for that push** (hard rule 2), and stop dead after the
88	  turn's final push (hard rule 3).
89	- The rung is committed by `vc-x1 push`, never pre-committed with `jj commit` (hard rule 1). Note
90	  `custom.md`: the installed binary predates the scope rename, so it takes `--scope=code|bot`.
91	- Read the checklist in `agent-data/cycle.md` immediately before acting, not from memory.
92	
93	## After this lands

95	Rebase `measure-reproducibility` (three commits, an in-flight cycle) onto `agent-files-model`, then
96	work its steps, refining the rules as they get used. Expect conflicts in `TODO.md`,
97	`notes/chores/chores-06.md` and `custom.md`, since this step and 0.24.1 rewrote all three. No
98	`src/` conflicts. The `custom.md` conflict is the interesting one: it forces the reclassification
99	test on real content.

title alone. Its own record is chores-06 `## docs: steps are titles, versions are stamps`, with the

version, a concise stamp that also gave the steps their order. A step
is one commit of a cycle. The problem is that a version can change at
any time, and preserving the order then forces a matching change
through every version after it.

This change removes the version from the record, leaving a step
defined by its title alone, so inserting or reordering a step has no
effect on any other step. Order now comes from a rung's position in
its ladder. The one version still written down sits on a chores
as-built rung beside that commit's SHA, where it describes a landed
commit rather than naming a step.

Three rules follow from it, and one repair:

- a title must be unambiguous within its cycle and its chores file
- a Done entry is a bold title with sub-bullets, and a commit body is
  a problem statement plus a solution statement
- a topic bookmark is a draft, so its ladder stays self-consistent
  until it lands
- the dynamic warmup ladder is backfilled, eight rungs whose commits
  landed on main two cycles ago

470	+### Steps are named, not numbered
471	+
472	+A step has a title and no number. Nothing in a ladder rung, a chores as-built rung, a `## Done`
473	+entry, or a commit gives a step an ordinal: a rung's place in the list already *is* its place in
474	+the ladder, so a number beside it would restate the position and then have to be maintained.
475	+
476	+- **The title is the identifier.** A record points at a step by its title, a plain greppable
477	+  mention, which is why the title is verbatim-identical across the three surfaces.
478	+- **Unambiguous, not globally unique.** Two titles must be distinguishable in the two places a
479	+  title is resolved: within its own cycle, so a ladder rung names one step, and within its chores
480	+  file, since a `##` header is also an anchor and a repeated slug silently dedupes to the first
481	+  one. Across the repo's history a title may repeat.
482	+- **Nothing renumbers.** Inserting, reordering or dropping a step edits the ladder list and
483	+  nothing else. On an unlanded topic bookmark the rungs that already committed an older ladder
484	+  come along; see
485	+  [Topic bookmarks are drafts](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts).
486	+- **`## Todo` ranks are the exception that stays numbered**, because a priority list has an order
487	+  worth reading off (see [Todo format](notes.md#todo-format)). Those numbers are positional too,
488	+  and are equally never used as references.
489	+
490	+### Versions live in the version-of-record only
491	+
492	+No version appears in durable prose: not in an in-flight ladder rung, a chores header, a
493	+`## Done` entry, `done.md`, a commit title, or a commit body. The manifest is the version's only
494	+written home (see [versioning.md](../notes/versioning.md)), and a commit's version is read from
495	+that file at that commit.
496	+
497	+**Why:** the version is a build stamp answering "which commit produced this artifact", not a name
498	+for a step. Written into prose it becomes a second identifier that history is free to invalidate:
499	+one renumber of published versions turns every prose mention, transcript and pasted report into
500	+residue that needs a decoder to read. A renumber cannot touch a title.
501	+
502	+**The one exception is a chores as-built rung**, which records a version alongside that commit's
503	+SHA once the commit is on a permanent branch. There the version is not naming a step: it is a
504	+recorded property of a landed commit, the same species as the SHA beside it, and the pair doubles
505	+as the decoder for an old `-V` banner or a pasted report. It obeys the SHA's timing exactly, so a
506	+rung on an unlanded branch carries neither (see
507	+[Chores commit references](notes.md#chores-commit-references)).
508	+
509	+**How to apply:** name the step by its title and the phase in words ("the close-out", "the
510	+opening"). Writing *about* versioning is unaffected: a version named as a specimen, whether in the
511	+scheme's own notation, a decoder table, or a narrative about a renumber, is a use of the word
512	+rather than an identifier for a step, the same distinction
513	+[Typeable punctuation only](#typeable-punctuation-only) draws between naming a character and using
514	+one. Existing versioned prose is grandfathered and converts when touched, no sweep.
515	+

664	+  because nothing is written yet
665	+- **titles must be unambiguous, not globally unique**, which is a weaker constraint than the first
666	+  draft of this rule carried. A title is resolved in exactly two places, so those are its scopes:
667	+  within its cycle, so a ladder rung names one step, and within its chores file, since a `##`
668	+  header is also an anchor and GitHub silently resolves a duplicate slug to the first occurrence.
669	+  Across history a title may repeat, and `git log --grep` returning two hits is not a defect
670	+- **a commit body is a problem statement and a solution statement**, both broad, and nothing else.
671	+  The dual-repo model is what makes that safe rather than lossy: the `ochid:` trailer reaches the
672	+  session that reasoned the change out, the as-built rung reaches this file, and the `## Todo`
673	+  entry holds the plan. See [The body took two passes too](#the-body-took-two-passes-too)
674	+- **a topic bookmark is a draft until it lands.** Keeping its series self-consistent may rewrite
675	+  rungs that are already pushed, which is legal because pushing to a bookmark is not publishing.
676	+  The mechanism is content amendment plus a force-push, never a re-describe, so the
677	+  never-re-describe rule and the `ochid:` trailers are both untouched (change ids survive a
678	+  rewrite, as the 2026-07-31 trapezoid experiment measured). Three exceptions are named in the
679	+  protocol so "when practical" is not re-litigated each time
680	+
681	+### How the numbering got to zero
682	+
683	+The rule arrived in three passes in one session, and the path is worth keeping because each pass
684	+removed something the previous one had assumed was needed.
685	+
686	+- **First**, versions came out of prose and ladder rungs took a `step-N` prefix in their place,
687	+  numbered positionally like a `## Todo` rank. That fixed the fragility but kept a number.
688	+- **Second**, the question was whether `step-N` should *be* the manifest's suffix, one numbering
689	+  serving both. Rejected: it rewrites the suffix scheme (the final-`0`-marks-a-Preparation rule,
690	+  the nesting notation, the disambiguation cases) to buy an agreement nothing reads.
691	+- **Third** (wink), the number went away entirely. A rung sits in an ordered markdown list, so
692	+  the number was restating the list position and adding a maintenance obligation, and the
693	+  renumber-on-insert rule the second pass needed was work invented by the first pass. What
694	+  survives is the part that was doing the job: the title.
695	+
696	+The cost, accepted rather than argued away: naming a step in conversation is now "the report
697	+renderer step" instead of "step-3", which is longer to say and cannot be ambiguous inside one
698	+cycle. The residue is that `versioning.md`'s suffix is the last number standing, and it is now
699	+explicit there that it names nothing.
700	+
701	+### The version was also a landmark, which is how the Done entries got reshaped
702	+
703	+Found by wink reading this very step: scanning `TODO.md > ## Done` for the new entry meant looking
704	+for `0.24.2`, not finding it, and concluding the entry was missing. It was there. The version had
705	+been doing a second job nobody had credited it with, a short high-contrast token per entry that
706	+the eye could rest on, and removing it exposed what it had been masking.
707	+
708	+The fix is not to restore it, because it was a poor landmark: its absence reported that a predicted
709	+number was missing, not that an entry was. A title answers the question a skim is actually asking.
710	+So the entries changed shape instead.
711	+
712	+- **A `## Done` entry is now a bold title line plus sub-bullets** (`agent-data/notes.md`
713	+  [Done entry form](../../agent-data/notes.md#done-entry-form)), matching the `## In Progress`
714	+  block, whose title line was already bold.
715	+- **The old form violated `prose.md` and had done so for a while.** A title with five lines of
716	+  summary trailing off it is the wall-of-prose shape Prose form warns about, and two rules still
717	+  called these entries one-liners (`notes.md`'s migration step and cycle-protocol's Close-out)
718	+  while `prose.md` separately blessed the paragraph. The version was hiding a drift, not
719	+  preventing one; all three now agree.
720	+- **The three live entries were converted**, versions dropped from the two older ones too, at
721	+  wink's call, so the section can be judged in its new form rather than in a mixture. `done.md`'s
722	+  existing entries stay under grandfathering.
723	+
724	+Bounded on purpose: Done and `done.md` entries are the only surface where a long body hangs off a
725	+title in a flat list. Chores as-built ladders got *more* skimmable, since a rung is one short line
726	+that lost a token, and `## Todo` keeps its ranks.
727	+
728	+### The body took two passes too
729	+
730	+The first pass kept the body an edit list. It said "one bullet per *distinct change*, not per
731	+file", called itself "source of truth for the mechanical edit list", and carried sub-rules for
732	+when files share a gist, when to name a glob, and when to switch to a count. That was already an
733	+improvement on one-bullet-per-file, and it survived exactly one use: writing this commit's own
734	+description produced thirteen bullets that restated `git show --stat` in worse English.
735	+
736	+The second pass (wink) dropped the list. A body is a **problem statement** then a **solution
737	+statement**, in broad terms, and the diff is left to be the mechanical record it already is.
738	+
739	+- **The first pass contradicted itself**, which is visible in the text it replaced: the rule
740	+  warned that "restating what `git show --stat` already prints is a second copy that can drift"
741	+  and then required a per-change list, which is the same duplication at a coarser grain.
742	+- **The glob and count sub-rules existed only to manage the list.** With no list they have no
743	+  job, so the rule got shorter rather than more qualified.
744	+- **The problem statement has to answer for what it takes away.** Writing this one surfaced the
745	+  test now in the rule: the problem said the version supplied the ordering, so the solution owed
746	+  the reader what supplies it now. A body that raises a question and leaves it is not concise, it
747	+  is incomplete.
748	+- **A knock-on correction**, found by the same review: `notes.md` justified chores carrying no
749	+  edit list on the ground that the *commit body* was the mechanical record. That was never quite
750	+  right and is now plainly wrong, and the file already had the better formulation a few lines
751	+  later ("Git owns the mechanical record"). It is now a three-way split: the diff is mechanical,
752	+  the body is problem and solution, chores is the design thinking.
753	+- **Four contradictions were cleared in the same pass**, all of them ours and most of them
754	+  introduced earlier the same day: the body rule stated in full in two files, `prose.md` still
755	+  calling bodies "file-by-file" in one place while forbidding it in another, two examples teaching
756	+  the abandoned shape, and the title length limit reading `<=50` in the authority file against
757	+  `<=72` in three others. The 50 stands, and body wrap stays 72.
758	+
759	+Then the pair turned out not to be new (wink). `prose.md` already had a `### Problem + plan shape`
760	+for `## In Progress` blocks, chores intros and `## Todo` entries, glossing its problem statement as
761	+"(the why)", which is what a problem statement is. So the commit body is that same shape in past
762	+tense: **tense picks the second half**, a plan for work ahead, a solution for work done. One
763	+`### Problem-first shape` now covers four surfaces, and the commit-body bullet keeps only what is
764	+commit-specific.
765	+
766	+The consolidation immediately caught a term collision we had been carrying. The shape section
767	+glosses the problem statement as "the why", while the body rule said "the *why* and *how* stay
768	+out", so the same word both belonged and did not. What actually stays out is the **deliberation**:
769	+alternatives weighed, evidence, dates, costs accepted. The problem is a why and belongs in the
770	+body. Two files said the wrong thing and now say that one.
771	+
772	+### The dynamic-warmup backfill, two cycles late
773	+
774	+This step also clears backfill debt, which is in scope because a close-out is where the checklist
775	+puts it and because the debt is what the new rule is about. `## feat: dynamic warmup`'s eight rungs
776	+sat on literal `[[N]]` placeholders even though the trapezoid rewrite had landed all eight on
777	+`main`, where their SHAs and versions were final. They are now filled, refs `[3]` through `[10]`.
778	+
779	+Why it was missed is the interesting part, and it is our own reported finding coming back: on
780	+2026-07-31 we told the family that the per-commit checklist has no step for backfilling the
781	+previous push's chores refs, and the 20260802 baseline answered it by adding per-commit step 4,
782	+"Close the records". We have not synced that baseline, so the gap we reported stayed open here and
783	+the next close-out skipped the same step. Backfill lives only in our close-out checklist, at step
784	+6, which is easy to reach the end of a docs cycle without reading.
785	+
786	+`## docs: experiment in the local agent-files` is *not* backfilled, correctly: it sits on the
787	+unlanded `agent-files-model`, so its rung keeps the placeholder, and under the timing rule above
788	+its `0.24.1` came out of the rung until the bookmark lands.
789	+
790	+Reference slots `[3]`..`[10]` were allocated next-free rather than by re-packing the file into
791	+document order, which would have renumbered the two design citations for cosmetics.
792	+
793	+### Grandfathering, and what deliberately keeps its versions
794	+
795	+Versioned prose already in the repo is not swept; it converts when its surrounding text is
796	+touched, the same treatment the legacy `Commits:` lines got. Two cases are deliberate rather than
797	+pending:
798	+
799	+- **`custom.md`'s 2026-08-01 renumber entry keeps its version mapping.** It *is* the decoder for
800	+  the residue, so stripping the versions out of it would defeat its purpose.
801	+- **the previous commit's body keeps its version-bump bullet.** It is published on this bookmark
802	+  and a body is not editable text; the rule applies from here forward rather than backwards.
803	+
804	+### Drafted before the rebase, on purpose
805	+
806	+The step lands on `agent-files-model` ahead of rebasing `measure-reproducibility` onto it, so the
807	+next cycle runs its ladder under these rules and the family reply carries evidence instead of
808	+intent. Refinements the dogfood turns up are collected in `TODO.md` and land as a later batch
809	+step, rather than each one triggering another rebase of the in-flight rungs.
810	+

## Close-out checklist

The cycle's last step, per the protocol's
[Close-out](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#close-out):

1. Move the picked-up item from `## In Progress` to a `## Done` entry: a bold title line with its
   chores `[N]` ref, detail as sub-bullets (see
   [Done entry form](notes.md#done-entry-form)).
2. Finalize the chores section: sync the header to the final commit title (and every anchor
   back-reference), add design subsections; the intro and As-built rungs are already there.
3. Full validation, mandatory.
4. Update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.
5. At push time, surface the shape options (squash / trapezoid / keep separate) and wait for
   the user's choice. The trapezoid recipe is
   [in the protocol](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#trapezoid-close-out-recipe); its step 4 is
   `jj git push`, not `vc-x1 push`.
6. Backfill the chores as-built ladder refs (and any remaining legacy `Commits:` lines) for
   the commits the previous push made permanent; never record a SHA that is not on a permanent
   branch.

## vc-x1 push behaviors to keep in mind

Three, independent of project language:

- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 assumes nothing about a repo's contents beyond
  `.jj` and `.vc-config.toml`, and runs no build or tests. The medium's validation is the
  per-commit flow's job, run *before* invoking `vc-x1 push`. The one check that remains is
  `push-work` verifying the bookmark's remote refs are tracked, which is its own precondition.
- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume. Every stage no-ops when its
  work is already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If a run fails, push stops and
  reports; getting the repos back to a sensible state is the user's call, not something the
  tool infers.
- **ochid trailers** are injected by `vc-x1 push` itself, so don't hand-write them into the
  commit body or `--title`/`--body`.

## Terms

Three names, used as defined here across
[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md),
[cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md), and the notes files:

- **version**: the per-commit version (e.g. `0.3.0-5.3.0`). It lives in the manifest and
  nowhere else. No ladder, chores section, todo entry, commit title, or commit body writes one
  (see
  [Versions live in the version-of-record only](../agent-data/prose.md#versions-live-in-the-version-of-record-only)),
  and its suffix encodes the cycle phase for whoever inspects the manifest (see
  [Suffix scheme](#suffix-scheme)).
- **version-of-record**: the authoritative stored copy of the version, in the project's manifest
  (see [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record)); a built or running
  artifact derives from it.
- **versioning**: the topic, this scheme as a whole.

## A stamp, not a name

The version answers "which commit produced this artifact". It is not a name for a step: a step is
named by its title and located by its position in the ladder list (see
[Steps are named, not numbered](../agent-data/prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)). So the
suffix below is the only number in the system, and since nothing dereferences it, reordering or
inserting a step leaves the versions already committed alone.

content.content:
335	What replaces them, and why each record exists:
336	
337	- **the diff** between a member and the payload is the live proposal set. It needs no maintenance
338	  and cannot go stale, which a hand-kept status list would
339	- **the commit history** is the durable record, and it matters because the diff is ephemeral by
340	  construction: at convergence the diff empties and every trace of what was proposed goes with
341	  it. History keeps the date, the author, the rationale, and via the `ochid:` trailer the
342	  bot-repo session that reasoned it out. That is why an agent-file change wants its own commit:
343	  ridden along inside a feature commit, the rule change survives as one file-by-file bullet
344	- **the dogfood log** carries what neither can derive, the why and the status, and it is now
345	  in-flight entries only
346	
347	`custom.md` narrows to what cannot be family-wide, and the two kinds are worth separating because
348	only one is negotiable:
349	
350	- **medium-determined** content (our `cargo fmt` / `clippy` / `cargo test` / `cargo doc`

What replaces them, and why each record exists:

- **the diff** between a member and the payload is the live proposal set. It needs no maintenance
  and cannot go stale, which a hand-kept status list would
- **the commit history** is the durable record, and it matters because the diff is ephemeral by
  construction: at convergence the diff empties and every trace of what was proposed goes with
  it. History keeps the date, the author, the rationale, and via the `ochid:` trailer the
  bot-repo session that reasoned it out. That is why an agent-file change wants its own commit:
  ridden along inside a feature commit, the rule change survives as one file-by-file bullet
- **the dogfood log** carries what neither can derive, the why and the status, and it is now
  in-flight entries only

`custom.md` narrows to what cannot be family-wide, and the two kinds are worth separating because
only one is negotiable:

- **medium-determined** content (our `cargo fmt` / `clippy` / `cargo test` / `cargo doc`
  validation commands) is not a divergence at all. A prose repo could not adopt them if it wanted
  to, so there is nothing to converge on and no pushback is possible
- **elective divergence** is where wink's pushback belongs, and the test is structural rather
  than dependent on anyone noticing: an entry must say why it cannot be family-wide. With no
  answer it is an experiment, and it belongs in the pinned file where the rule lives

from proposed by reading it, which the pinned/`custom.md` split used to do structurally. Our own

### Typeable punctuation only

Durable text uses punctuation that can be typed at a terminal. Banned: `—`, `–`, `…`, `→`.
None can be entered without a compose key or a paste, so none can be grepped for, and an em
dash next to option syntax reads as another flag. Unlike the semicolon rule above this one is
absolute: they cost nothing to write and are paid on every read, so a soft rule accumulates
them.

`…` becomes `...` and `→` becomes `->`. The dashes have no single replacement, because an em
dash usually stands in for a structural decision that was not made. Make the decision:

- **A bullet's title and its body sharing a line** is a heading and a paragraph. Make the body
  sub-bullets.
- **A term and its definition** (`jj diff`, `<base>`, a flag) takes a colon, which keeps a
  glossary or a command list at one line per entry.
- **A prose aside** takes a comma, parentheses, or two sentences. Often the aside should just
  go.

Converting a heading moves its anchor. The em dash strips but the spaces on both sides survive,
so `## A — B` slugs to `#a--b` while its colon form slugs to `#a-b` (see
[Markdown anchor links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links)). Re-point inbound links in the same
commit.

Scope is the same as [Speculation marker](#speculation-marker), plus commit titles and
everything under `src/`: doc comments, inline comments, and any user-visible string. Source is
the surface a human edits and greps most, so an untypeable character costs more there than in
prose. It applies going forward; existing text converts when touched. A code span is not exempt
by itself. Naming the character is a specimen and stays, which is how this section names them.
A banned character doing a job is a use and converts: `` `.expect(…)` `` becomes
`` `.expect(...)` ``.

Text quoted from outside this repo's prose (tool output, an error message, an already-published
commit title) is transcribed, not written, so it keeps its characters, whether or not it sits
in a code span. It matters most for commit titles: converting one stops it matching
`git log --grep` and breaks the verbatim identity that
[Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--chores--commit) requires between
a commit title, its chores header, and its `## Done` entry.

The Terms bullet needs the exception named or "chores section" dropped from the enumeration. 9. Nit: the body says "Three rules follow from it, and one repair" but its second bullet packs two rules (Done entry form and commit body form).

# Versioning

How this project versions its commits and the running artifact. The scheme, meaning the manifest's
suffix spelling and the unique-per-commit aim, is generic and shared across projects: this file is
copied **verbatim**, with
[Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record) covering each medium by
conditional rather than per-project edits.

## Terms

Three names, used as defined here across
[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md),
[cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md), and the notes files:

- **version**: the per-commit version (e.g. `0.3.0-5.3.0`). It lives in the manifest and
  nowhere else. No ladder, chores section, todo entry, commit title, or commit body writes one
  (see
  [Versions live in the version-of-record only](../agent-data/prose.md#versions-live-in-the-version-of-record-only)),
  and its suffix encodes the cycle phase for whoever inspects the manifest (see
  [Suffix scheme](#suffix-scheme)).
- **version-of-record**: the authoritative stored copy of the version, in the project's manifest
  (see [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record)); a built or running
  artifact derives from it.
- **versioning**: the topic, this scheme as a whole.

## A stamp, not a name

The version answers "which commit produced this artifact". It is not a name for a step: a step is
named by its title and located by its position in the ladder list (see
[Steps are named, not numbered](../agent-data/prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)). So the
suffix below is the only number in the system, and since nothing dereferences it, reordering or
inserting a step leaves the versions already committed alone.

## Recording the version-of-record

Where the version-of-record lives, how it's stored and surfaced, and how often it changes. Pick
the case that fits your medium:

- **Manifest**, where the version-of-record is stored:
  - if Rust, `Cargo.toml` `[package].version`
  - if Python, `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` (or the committed config it's sourced from)
  - otherwise wherever the medium records it (a generic `version.toml`, a book's frontmatter,
    ...); add the case as needed
- **Notation**, how the `-` form is stored:
  - if the format allows `-` (TOML `version.toml`, `Cargo.toml`), store it verbatim
  - if it bars `-` (PEP 440's local segment, e.g. a Python project), remap to `+`, so
    `0.3.0-5.3.0` becomes `0.3.0+5.3.0`: same version, just the stored spelling
- **Reporter**, how a built artifact surfaces the version-of-record:
  - if a CLI app, `<cli-app> -V`
  - if a TUI/GUI, add to Help/About or display on the title
- **Cadence**, how often to bump: see
  [Unique per commit](#unique-per-commit-preference-not-requirement); this project follows the
  per-commit preference.

## Unique per commit (preference, not requirement)

Our general notion is that the version-of-record should change on **every commit**, so a built or
running artifact identifies the exact commit it came from.

- This is a preference, **not** a hard requirement. A project following the cycle protocol may
  bump less often: once per cycle, only at release, and so on. Record the choice in
  [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record) if it differs.
- It is achievable because the cycle's versions (below) are **pre-assignable**, unlike the git
  SHA, which a commit cannot contain (see the cycle protocol's
  [Commits backfill](cycle-protocol.md#commits-backfill)).

## Suffix scheme

The cycle (Preparation -> Work -> Close-out; see [cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md)) encodes
each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a Preparation**.

This is the manifest's own spelling, read by whoever inspects `Cargo.toml` or `-V` output. It is
not a name for a step: a step is identified by its title, and an in-flight ladder rung carries
neither a number nor a version (see
[Steps are named, not numbered](../agent-data/prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)). The one
prose surface that records a version is a chores as-built rung, where it is a property of a landed
commit sitting beside that commit's SHA. The identifiers below count commits within a phase;
nothing dereferences one.

- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: Work commits
- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)

**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0`
and starts at `-1` (its first Work commit). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle needing no
Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that grows a Preparation later adds the `0` step
without renumbering siblings.

Disambiguation:

- `-10`: Work commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a Preparation.
- `-1.0`: Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final identifier `0`).

**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:

- `X.Y.Z-3.0`: Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle
- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2`: its Work
- `X.Y.Z-3`: its Close-out
- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0`: Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle

Bump the version-of-record at the start of each phase, so the active phase is recorded and, per
the preference above, every commit carries a distinct version.

Previously a step was named twice in the records, by a title and by a
version, a concise stamp that also gave the steps their order. A step
is one commit of a cycle. The problem is that a version can change at
any time, and preserving the order then forces a matching change
through every version after it.

This change removes the version from the record, leaving a step
defined by its title alone, so inserting or reordering a step has no
effect on any other step. Order now comes from a rung's position in
its ladder. The one version still written down sits on a chores
as-built rung beside that commit's SHA, where it describes a landed
commit rather than naming a step.

Four rules follow from it, and one repair:

- a title must be unambiguous within its cycle and its chores file
- a Done entry is a bold title with sub-bullets
- a commit body is a problem statement plus a solution statement
- a topic bookmark is a draft, so its ladder stays self-consistent
  until it lands
- the dynamic warmup ladder is backfilled, eight rungs whose commits
  landed on main two cycles ago

content.text:
Where it's defined today — the answer is "mostly in the dogfood log, not the protocol":

- **custom.md:179-198** is the real authority: the 2026-07-31 adopted rule ("every commit belongs to a cycle, single- or multi-commit... ask 'single- or multi-step cycle?' before preparing the commit. A single-commit cycle is a bare `X.Y.Z` close-out, so its validation is mandatory... skips `## In Progress`"), plus the same-day Todo #1 entry that carries the only *shape test* ("multi-commit wants rungs that each stand alone; 'one deliverable, several files' is single-commit shaped no matter how many edits it takes").
- **agent-data/notes.md:227** has one consequence: a single-commit cycle's chores ladder is a one-rung ladder whose rung is the close-out.
- **notes/cycle-protocol.md** — the file that claims to be the authority on cycles — only mentions single-commit cycles in passing (line 62, the chores rung; line 620, a version note). It never defines the distinction or the decision test.
- **agent-data/cycle.md** doesn't mention it at all.

So your instinct is right, and the situation is actually one notch worse than "at a glance implies it": the distinction is defined *only* in a project-local dogfood entry, scattered across two 2026-07-31 bullets, while the pinned protocol is silent. Anyone reading the pinned set alone would conclude every cycle has separate commits.

On the reframing itself — I think it's correct, and the repo's own practice is the evidence. The pending 0.24.2 step did all three phases' work: it bumped the version-of-record (Preparation), made the change (Work), and wrote the chores section, Done entry, and mandatory validation (Close-out) — in one commit. The existing rule already half-says this: "a single-commit cycle is its own close-out, so validation is mandatory" only makes sense if the one commit *is* the close-out phase, not a cycle that skipped it. Your framing — **phases describe the work, commits describe the publication granularity** — makes that explicit instead of accidental.

Two things I'd add to it:

1. **It unifies three special cases the docs currently treat separately.** The "lightweight cycle" (versioning.md:84, Preparation "omitted") becomes "Preparation's work rides in the first Work commit" — the version still gets bumped, the todo still gets picked up, so the phase happened, uncommitted. The squash-form sub-cycle is the same collapse one level down: phases happen as scratch commits, then fuse into one at close-out. And the single-commit cycle is the full collapse at top level. One principle (phases always happen; what varies is how many commits they're cut into, and the cut test is "does each rung stand alone") replaces three "optional/skipped" carve-outs.

2. **One nuance to keep the reframe honest**: some artifacts genuinely don't exist in the collapsed form — the `## In Progress` block is skipped, not just uncommitted. That's consistent with your model rather than against it, but worth stating: In Progress is *cross-commit* state, tracking a ladder between pushes, so a one-commit cycle has no "between" for it to track. The phase's work (deciding the plan) still happens; the artifact only exists where there's state to carry.

Where it should land: cycle-protocol.md is the stated authority, so the definition belongs there — the three-phases-always-happen framing, the single/multi distinction, the stand-alone-rung test, and the ask-before-preparing rule — with cycle.md's "at a glance" carrying a one-sentence summary as you suggest. That move also graduates the custom.md 2026-07-31 rule out of the dogfood log, which is overdue on its own terms (under the new contract it's an experiment that belongs in the pinned file where the rule lives), and it's convergence-relevant: vc-x1's tier-2 agenda already lists "every commit belongs to a cycle" as a cycle-protocol.md candidate and notes their "interludes" are your single-commit cycles under another name. So writing it into the local pinned files would be exactly the new proposal mechanism working.

Process-wise it's an agent-file/protocol change, so it wants its own commit — not folded into the pending step, which is complete and reviewed. It would make a fitting next single-commit cycle (self-demonstrating), or a `## Todo` entry now if you'd rather batch it with the post-dogfood refinements.

The plain version: single- vs multi-step cycles are currently defined only in custom.md's dogfood log, and the official protocol file never defines them — your reframing (every cycle has all three phases; a single-step cycle just does them in one commit instead of several) is right, matches how the repo actually works, and would replace three scattered "optional" exceptions with one rule. It deserves its own small commit into cycle-protocol.md and cycle.md, and it doubles as a family proposal vc-x1 is already asking for. Happy to draft it when you want; not touching anything now.

# Cycle checklists

Checklists for the moments where slips happen: committing, pushing, closing out. The full
protocol, with rationale and recovery procedures, is
[cycle-protocol.md](../notes/cycle-protocol.md); on any disagreement, that file wins. Re-read
the relevant checklist immediately before the action; don't run it from memory.

Universal file, shared with the template repository; a proposed change is edited here and
converges at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
Project-local content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).

## The cycle at a glance

Every change runs as a **cycle**: an optional Preparation step -> Work steps -> a Close-out
step, one commit each. The ladder lists them in order and identifies each by its title, with no
number and no version; where the version-of-record lives and how often it is bumped are in
[versioning.md](../notes/versioning.md). Read
[cycle-protocol.md](../notes/cycle-protocol.md) before any commit work, and before any push,
cycle or not.

## Committing vs pushing

A cycle rung is committed *by* `vc-x1 push`; never pre-commit it with `jj commit`. Push's
commit stages commit both repos with the approved title/body and stamp each new commit's
`ochid:` trailer (see [ochid trailers](jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)); a
pre-committed rung leaves `@` empty and push mints a stamped empty duplicate (bugs.md #6). In
an instruction, "commit", "push", and "commit + push" all mean `vc-x1 push`. A bare `jj commit`
is asked for by name ("local commit", "just `jj commit`") and is only for work that never
publishes (local-only saves and loop-and-squash intermediates), with no `ochid:`. The approval
around a push, interactive by default and waived only by an explicit scoped delegation, is the
cycle protocol's [Pushing policy](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#policy).

## Topic bookmarks are drafts

A topic bookmark is a draft until it lands on a permanent branch; pushed there is not published.
So keep the series inside it self-consistent: inserting or reordering a step edits the ladder in
the rungs that already committed an older version of it, not only at the tip.

- **Amend content, never re-describe.** Editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not a
  `jj describe`, so hard rule 4 stays intact and the `ochid:` trailers ride along untouched
  (they carry change ids, which survive a rewrite).
- **Then force-push the bookmark**, under the same approval as any other push.
- **Exceptions, where self-consistency is not worth its cost**: the bookmark has already landed;
  another branch is stacked on it, so the rewrite becomes someone else's rebase; or the ladder
  is long and only a trailing snapshot disagrees.

The squash-form ladder below never meets this, since nothing on it is pushed. The rule is for the
multi-commit shape, whose rungs publish one at a time. Full statement in the protocol's
[Topic bookmarks are drafts](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts).

## Per-commit checklist

Every commit (Preparation, each Work commit, Close-out), per the protocol's
[Per-commit flow](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow):

1. Mark the rung `(current)` in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, as the first edit.
2. Do the work. On any deviation from the agreed plan, or any question, stop and surface it.
3. Flip `(current)` -> `(done)`, before validation and the commit.
4. Validate the artifact (the medium-specific commands are in [custom.md](../custom.md)).
   Skip-able for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out.
5. Say "ready to commit" and stop. The user reviews the working-copy diff; iterate until
   complete.
6. Write the description: a <=50-col conventional title, then a problem statement and a solution
   statement, both broad, wrapped at <=72. No version in either, no file list (the diff is the
   mechanical record), and no deliberation (chores, todo, and the session hold that). See
   [Commit description](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#commit-description).
7. Show title + body and stop for review. This review covers the push only when the user's go
   explicitly includes it.
8. On the user's go: `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --title "..." --body "..."`. Never pre-commit with
   `jj commit`; never hand-write `ochid:` trailers.

## Ladder (sub-cycle) checklist

Within a sub-cycle ladder, per the protocol's
[per-Work-commit contract](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#per-work-commit-contract-within-a-ladder):

1. `jj new -R .`: fresh empty `@`.
2. Do the commit's work.
3. Run the fast validation (named in [custom.md](../custom.md)). Non-negotiable.
4. `jj describe -m "..." -m "..." -R .`: scratch working title. This first-time authoring is
   the one permitted describe; the commit is never published and never carries a trailer.

Nothing on a ladder is pushed; the close-out squash
(`jj squash --from "<base>..@-" --into @ -u -R .`) collapses it, and `vc-x1 push` then
publishes the single commit.

## Before any push

- This specific push has the user's explicit approval. Approval of a plan that includes a push
  is not push approval; "commit and push" names the destination, not a waiver of the reviews.
  Only an explicit scoped delegation ("do all of X, don't check in") waives the stops, for that
  bounded task only; destructive ops still pause.
- Validation ran, and passed, after the last edit.
- Closing words are already written; nothing follows the turn's final push (next checklist).

## After the final push: hard stop

Once the turn's final push or bot-repo squash-push is invoked, do no further work: no
verification, no summary, no next-step offers, no edits, until the user speaks. Put all closing
words *before* the invoke. The harness rejects an empty turn, so it may force a visible token
after the tool returns; if so, emit a bare acknowledgment only (e.g. "landed"), never a summary
or more work. Post-push verification happens next turn at the user's direction. A standing
delegation makes intermediate pushes just steps; the hard stop lands on the turn's *final*
push. See
[After push or squash-push](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#after-push-or-squash-push-stop-and-wait).

## Close-out checklist

The cycle's last step, per the protocol's
[Close-out](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#close-out):

1. Move the picked-up item from `## In Progress` to a `## Done` entry: a bold title line with its
   chores `[N]` ref, detail as sub-bullets (see
   [Done entry form](notes.md#done-entry-form)).
2. Finalize the chores section: sync the header to the final commit title (and every anchor
   back-reference), add design subsections; the intro and As-built rungs are already there.
3. Full validation, mandatory.
4. Update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.
5. At push time, surface the shape options (squash / trapezoid / keep separate) and wait for
   the user's choice. The trapezoid recipe is
   [in the protocol](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#trapezoid-close-out-recipe); its step 4 is
   `jj git push`, not `vc-x1 push`.
6. Backfill the chores as-built ladder refs (and any remaining legacy `Commits:` lines) for
   the commits the previous push made permanent; never record a SHA that is not on a permanent
   branch.

## vc-x1 push behaviors to keep in mind

Three, independent of project language:

- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 assumes nothing about a repo's contents beyond
  `.jj` and `.vc-config.toml`, and runs no build or tests. The medium's validation is the
  per-commit flow's job, run *before* invoking `vc-x1 push`. The one check that remains is
  `push-work` verifying the bookmark's remote refs are tracked, which is its own precondition.
- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume. Every stage no-ops when its
  work is already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If a run fails, push stops and
  reports; getting the repos back to a sensible state is the user's call, not something the
  tool infers.
- **ochid trailers** are injected by `vc-x1 push` itself, so don't hand-write them into the
  commit body or `--title`/`--body`.

# Cycle checklists

Checklists for the moments where slips happen: committing, pushing, closing out. The full
protocol, with rationale and recovery procedures, is
[cycle-protocol.md](../notes/cycle-protocol.md); on any disagreement, that file wins. Re-read
the relevant checklist immediately before the action; don't run it from memory.

Universal file, shared with the template repository; a proposed change is edited here and
converges at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
Project-local content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).

## The cycle at a glance

Every change runs as a **cycle** with three phases: Preparation -> Work -> Close-out. The
phases always happen; what a cycle chooses is commit granularity. A **multi-step** cycle
commits them individually, as a ladder of steps (the Preparation commit is optional); a
**single-step** cycle folds all three into one commit when the change is straightforward, so
that one commit is the close-out and carries its duties, mandatory validation included. The
ladder lists a cycle's steps in order and identifies each by its title, with no number and no
version; where the version-of-record lives and how often it is bumped are in
[versioning.md](../notes/versioning.md). Read
[cycle-protocol.md](../notes/cycle-protocol.md) before any commit work, and before any push,
cycle or not.

## Committing vs pushing

A cycle rung is committed *by* `vc-x1 push`; never pre-commit it with `jj commit`. Push's
commit stages commit both repos with the approved title/body and stamp each new commit's
`ochid:` trailer (see [ochid trailers](jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)); a
pre-committed rung leaves `@` empty and push mints a stamped empty duplicate (bugs.md #6). In
an instruction, "commit", "push", and "commit + push" all mean `vc-x1 push`. A bare `jj commit`
is asked for by name ("local commit", "just `jj commit`") and is only for work that never
publishes (local-only saves and loop-and-squash intermediates), with no `ochid:`. The approval
around a push, interactive by default and waived only by an explicit scoped delegation, is the
cycle protocol's [Pushing policy](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#policy).

## Topic bookmarks are drafts

A topic bookmark is a draft until it lands on a permanent branch; pushed there is not published.
So keep the series inside it self-consistent: inserting or reordering a step edits the ladder in
the rungs that already committed an older version of it, not only at the tip.

- **Amend content, never re-describe.** Editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not a
  `jj describe`, so hard rule 4 stays intact and the `ochid:` trailers ride along untouched
  (they carry change ids, which survive a rewrite).
- **Then force-push the bookmark**, under the same approval as any other push.
- **Exceptions, where self-consistency is not worth its cost**: the bookmark has already landed;
  another branch is stacked on it, so the rewrite becomes someone else's rebase; or the ladder
  is long and only a trailing snapshot disagrees.

The squash-form ladder below never meets this, since nothing on it is pushed. The rule is for the
multi-commit shape, whose rungs publish one at a time. Full statement in the protocol's
[Topic bookmarks are drafts](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts).

## Per-commit checklist

Every commit (Preparation, each Work commit, Close-out), per the protocol's
[Per-commit flow](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow):

1. Mark the rung `(current)` in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, as the first edit.
2. Do the work. On any deviation from the agreed plan, or any question, stop and surface it.
3. Flip `(current)` -> `(done)`, before validation and the commit.
4. Validate the artifact (the medium-specific commands are in [custom.md](../custom.md)).
   Skip-able for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out.
5. Say "ready to commit" and stop. The user reviews the working-copy diff; iterate until
   complete.
6. Write the description: a <=50-col conventional title, then a problem statement and a solution
   statement, both broad, wrapped at <=72. No version in either, no file list (the diff is the
   mechanical record), and no deliberation (chores, todo, and the session hold that). See
   [Commit description](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#commit-description).
7. Show title + body and stop for review. This review covers the push only when the user's go
   explicitly includes it.
8. On the user's go: `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --title "..." --body "..."`. Never pre-commit with
   `jj commit`; never hand-write `ochid:` trailers.

## Ladder (sub-cycle) checklist

Within a sub-cycle ladder, per the protocol's
[per-Work-commit contract](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#per-work-commit-contract-within-a-ladder):

1. `jj new -R .`: fresh empty `@`.
2. Do the commit's work.
3. Run the fast validation (named in [custom.md](../custom.md)). Non-negotiable.
4. `jj describe -m "..." -m "..." -R .`: scratch working title. This first-time authoring is
   the one permitted describe; the commit is never published and never carries a trailer.

Nothing on a ladder is pushed; the close-out squash
(`jj squash --from "<base>..@-" --into @ -u -R .`) collapses it, and `vc-x1 push` then
publishes the single commit.

## Before any push

- This specific push has the user's explicit approval. Approval of a plan that includes a push
  is not push approval; "commit and push" names the destination, not a waiver of the reviews.
  Only an explicit scoped delegation ("do all of X, don't check in") waives the stops, for that
  bounded task only; destructive ops still pause.
- Validation ran, and passed, after the last edit.
- Closing words are already written; nothing follows the turn's final push (next checklist).

## After the final push: hard stop

Once the turn's final push or bot-repo squash-push is invoked, do no further work: no
verification, no summary, no next-step offers, no edits, until the user speaks. Put all closing
words *before* the invoke. The harness rejects an empty turn, so it may force a visible token
after the tool returns; if so, emit a bare acknowledgment only (e.g. "landed"), never a summary
or more work. Post-push verification happens next turn at the user's direction. A standing
delegation makes intermediate pushes just steps; the hard stop lands on the turn's *final*
push. See
[After push or squash-push](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#after-push-or-squash-push-stop-and-wait).

## Close-out checklist

The cycle's last step, per the protocol's
[Close-out](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#close-out):

1. Move the picked-up item from `## In Progress` to a `## Done` entry: a bold title line with its
   chores `[N]` ref, detail as sub-bullets (see
   [Done entry form](notes.md#done-entry-form)).
2. Finalize the chores section: sync the header to the final commit title (and every anchor
   back-reference), add design subsections; the intro and As-built rungs are already there.
3. Full validation, mandatory.
4. Update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.
5. At push time, surface the shape options (squash / trapezoid / keep separate) and wait for
   the user's choice. The trapezoid recipe is
   [in the protocol](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#trapezoid-close-out-recipe); its step 4 is
   `jj git push`, not `vc-x1 push`.
6. Backfill the chores as-built ladder refs (and any remaining legacy `Commits:` lines) for
   the commits the previous push made permanent; never record a SHA that is not on a permanent
   branch.

## vc-x1 push behaviors to keep in mind

Three, independent of project language:

- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 assumes nothing about a repo's contents beyond
  `.jj` and `.vc-config.toml`, and runs no build or tests. The medium's validation is the
  per-commit flow's job, run *before* invoking `vc-x1 push`. The one check that remains is
  `push-work` verifying the bookmark's remote refs are tracked, which is its own precondition.
- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume. Every stage no-ops when its
  work is already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If a run fails, push stops and
  reports; getting the repos back to a sensible state is the user's call, not something the
  tool infers.
- **ochid trailers** are injected by `vc-x1 push` itself, so don't hand-write them into the
  commit body or `--title`/`--body`.

Body (all lines <=72):

```
Previously a step was named twice in the records, by a title and by a
version, a concise stamp that also gave the steps their order. A step
is one commit of a cycle. The problem is that a version can change at
any time, and preserving the order then forces a matching change
through every version after it.

This change removes the version from the record, leaving a step
defined by its title alone, so inserting or reordering a step has no
effect on any other step. Order now comes from a rung's position in
its ladder. The one version still written down sits on a chores
as-built rung beside that commit's SHA, where it describes a landed
commit rather than naming a step.

Four rules follow from it, and one repair:

- a title must be unambiguous within its cycle and its chores file
- a Done entry is a bold title with sub-bullets
- a commit body is a problem statement plus a solution statement
- a topic bookmark is a draft, so its ladder stays self-consistent
  until it lands
- the dynamic warmup ladder is backfilled, eight rungs whose commits
  landed on main two cycles ago
```

One thing for your review: the body doesn't mention the cycle.md at-a-glance rewrite (phases always happen, two styles) — that rode along as a review-pass improvement and isn't strictly a consequence of steps-are-titles. If you'd rather the body acknowledge it, a sixth bullet like `- a ride-along: cycle.md now states the two cycle styles, single- and multi-step, instead of implying them` would do it; otherwise the diff and this session's record carry it. Your call.

The push failed partway, on a network error — reporting and stopping per the checklist ("if a run fails, push stops and reports; getting the repos back to a sensible state is the user's call").

What happened, from the output:

- vc-x1 ran the **bot-repo stage first** (`squash-push-bot`): the local squash `@ -> @-` completed and the bot repo's `main` bookmark moved to the squashed commit.
- The **push to origin then died on the wire**: `send-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet` / `Connection to github.com closed by remote host` — a transient SSH/network failure (the X11-forwarding warnings are noise from the SSH config, not the cause).
- vc-x1 stopped there, so the **work-repo stage never ran**: no work-repo commit was created, nothing was pushed to either remote, and the working copy with the step is untouched.

cycle.md's "vc-x1 push behaviors" says rerunning is safe — push keeps no state, and every stage no-ops when its work is already done, so a re-run would skip the completed bot-repo squash and retry the pushes. The error pattern reads transient, so a plain re-run of the identical command is the likely fix.

Per the failure rule I'm not re-running on my own — say the word and I'll re-invoke the same push.

input.description: Show the byte size of the two session transcript files

content.text:
The data is modest: the pending bot-repo push is two session transcripts, 2.6 MB + 836 KB (~3.4 MB, and jsonl compresses well, so the actual pack is likely around a megabyte). GitHub handles pushes orders of magnitude larger than this over SSH without blinking, so I don't think GitHub or git itself is the problem — which points at your second suspect.

What the evidence says:

- The connection and SSH auth **succeed** — jj gets far enough to compute the bookmark move and git starts `send-pack`. The disconnect happens **mid-transfer** ("unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet"), twice, at the same stage.
- My shell runs inside Claude Code's sandbox, which routes network traffic through a filtering layer (github.com is allowlisted, but everything still passes through it). A connection that dies consistently once real data starts flowing, while small control traffic works, fits a sandbox proxy choking on the stream — and matches your observation that it fails "especially with long conversations", i.e., exactly when the transcript payload is biggest.
- Earlier small pushes succeeding and this one failing twice identically makes plain network flakiness unlikely.

The clean experiment: run the identical push **outside** the sandbox. I can't disable sandboxing from my side (policy), but you can run it in your own shell via the `!` prefix, which executes unsandboxed and lands the output in this conversation:

```
! vc-x1 push agent-files-model --title "$(cat tmp/title.txt)" --body "$(cat tmp/body.txt)"
```

Re-running is safe per vc-x1's design — the completed bot-repo squash stages will fold in and the pushes retry. If it succeeds from your shell, we've confirmed the sandbox is the culprit, and the durable fix is a sandbox/network setting for large SSH streams (or an HTTPS remote for the bot repo) rather than anything in vc-x1.
